correctness.rationale: The Euclidean successor-cluster lemma holds for arbitrary relations, including infinite, nonserial and nontransitive frames: every successor sees the same universal reflexive cluster. Hence the published BKS S5 translation can be applied at every immediate successor, and its replacement inside a maximal modal subformula preserves truth at any root. A propositional Boolean skeleton is polynomially compiled by standard balancing, and substituting S5 translations yields an explicit product-of-polynomials syntax-tree bound. The BKS Theorems 3.2/4.4 and Lemma 4.7 were inspected in the actual primary PDF. The included standalone verifier exhaustively checks all 354 Euclidean frames on 1–4 worlds and all one-variable valuations for four nontrivial modal substitution laws. Finite tests are corroboration, not the all-size proof. No unstated seriality/reflexivity assumption or normalization is used.

value.rationale: Whether non-locally-monotone Boolean connectives give exponentially shorter modal formulas depends sharply on accessibility-frame structure; recent 2026 work settles S4 and B negatively and transitive-symmetric frames positively. The K5 case is a canonical modal-logic frame class strictly broader than S5 and includes nontransitive Euclidean frames, so polynomial translation there is a substantive missing point in this landscape. The successor-cluster plus Boolean-skeleton transfer supplies reusable structural information and a uniform all-formulas size guarantee, not just a routine finite calculation. The exact optimal polynomial degree remains open.
